brief.topic: How tool calling actually works, in 30 seconds
brief.audience: PMs and leaders reviewing agent designs

coreInsight: In tool calling the model only proposes a call; your code decides whether and how to run it, so permissions, approvals and logging belong in your code, not the prompt.

hooks.text: The model doesn’t run your tools. Your code does.
hooks.notes: Corrects a common mental model that hides where control actually sits.

hooks.text: Who’s really in control of your AI agent?
hooks.notes: Good curiosity, but vague until later.

caption.opening: In tool calling, the model never presses the button. It asks your code to.
body:
The loop:
1. User asks
2. Model proposes a tool + arguments
3. Your code decides whether to run it
4. Result goes back to the model
5. Model writes the answer
That’s why permissions, approval gates and audit logs belong in your code. A prompt that says “don’t delete anything” is a request, not a control.
Review questions: which tools and scope? Which actions need a human? What happens on failure? Is every call logged?
